Lussekatter (Swedish Saffron Buns)

Served at: Lussinatta (St. Lucia's Vigil) · St. Lucia's Day

Makes about 20 bunsPrep 30 minCook 15 min

Lussekatter are traditional Swedish saffron buns baked and enjoyed during Lussinatta, the vigil of St. Lucia's Day on December 13th. These golden, sweet buns are shaped into elegant 'S' forms and symbolically represent light in the dark winter, honoring St. Lucia's role as a bearer of light.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk, warmed
  • 0.25 oz (7 g) active dry yeast
  • 0.5 tsp sugar
  • 0.5 tsp saffron threads
  • 0.25 cup (60 g) unsalted butter, melted
  • 0.75 cup (150 g) granulated sugar
  • 0.5 tsp salt
  • 3.5 cups (440 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1 large egg
  • Raisins for decoration

Method

  1. Warm the milk to about 100°F (38°C) and dissolve the yeast and sugar in it. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. Crush the saffron threads and steep them in 1 tablespoon of hot water for 5 minutes to release color and flavor.
  3. In a large bowl, combine the yeast mixture, saffron water, melted butter, sugar, salt, and egg. Mix well.
  4. Gradually add the flour, mixing until a soft dough forms. Knead on a floured surface for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  5. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a clean towel, and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour or until doubled in size.
  6. Punch down the dough and divide it into 20 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a long rope and shape into an 'S'.
  7. Place the shaped buns on baking sheets lined with parchment paper. Press a raisin into the center of each swirl.
  8. Cover the buns with a towel and let them rise for another 30 minutes.
  9. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  10. Brush the buns gently with a beaten egg for a glossy finish.
  11. Bake for 12-15 minutes until golden and puffed.
  12. Remove from oven and cool on wire racks before serving.

Tips

  • Use good quality saffron for the best flavor and vibrant color.
  • If you prefer a richer dough, substitute half the milk with cream.
  • For a festive touch, sprinkle pearl sugar on top before baking instead of egg wash.
